The Vairocana Chaos Table is not in V.3.1.

Heavenly Restriction or Heavenly Pact refers to a binding vow forced on a sorcerer's body at birth. This usually affects their cursed energy in exchange for limitations or improvements on their body. The most notable is the absolute physicality of Zenin Toji, but there are many different types of Heavenly Pacts. A creature can only have one Heavenly Pact. If the limitations of the Heavenly Pact are superseded, anything gained becomes null.

This is typically the first step in any tabletop RPG or D&D-styled game. Use your imagination to think up what type of character you want to be in this world. Make sure it remains mostly thematic regarding the setting, as this isn't a standard D&D campaign.

Think about what race you would like your character to be, their personality, goals, back story, specialties, career, appearance, traits, and relationships. Once you have all of these qualities decided, start following the steps below and writing everything down.

Using a "Character Sheet" provided by Wizards of the Coast for 5th Edition, you can track much of this. You may need to make a few modifications for certain things, like tracking your Domain Expansion.

Races in the Jujutsu Kaisen world are quite limited, mostly being between cursed spirits and humans. Deciding your race can be pretty important to describing your character's appearance and abilities, as well as occasionally defining their goals. Humans are easily the most common race to find when exploring the planet, Curses however are peculiar and in all shapes and sizes and limited to mostly Japan although rarely found outside. More information on these races is listed in Chapter 2.

Each character should specialize in a field while killing cursed spirits. A class will determine your prominent talents and skills, allowing your character to hone and grow their abilities throughout the adventure. For example, a brawler may focus mainly on fighting while a strategist can be useful in performing specific tasks outside of combat that may benefit the group, such as curtains. While having an all-around useful character is important, sometimes it doesn't hurt to have a character that tends to be extremely good at only one thing, so long as they benefit the group and feel fun to play. A well-rounded party can make the journey far more enjoyable in the long run.
Put some time into deciding what you want your character's role to be in the unit. Maybe discuss it with others in the group to see what would work best for everyone. However, make sure to choose something you will have fun with and appreciate. Once you have a general idea of what your class will be, pick from the classes listed in Chapter 3.

First, hopefully, you've already decided on a name for your character. If not, try to think of something you like the sound of. If you can't think of anything, feel free to look up D&D name generators online. Then, start to develop their personality and appearance in your head.

After you have a concept in mind, you want to start writing and organizing these ideas onto your character sheet. Try to find what Alignment best fits them and their morals. Then, start to think up some defining Personality Traits. Once you mark those down on your character sheet, start getting into their Ideals, Bonds, and Flaws. These will provide a guideline on how you plan on roleplaying and making decisions with your character.

Now you want to decide on your character's Background. Your background will provide you with tools and knowledge gained from how you've lived your life before the start of the campaign. This will affect how those who recognize you interact with you, how you're treated by the general public, and what your occupation is or was. A DM may provide you with custom backgrounds for this adventure, but feel free to choose from the ones listed in Chapter 4.

By exploring the World and fighting your way through various forces, your characters will start to develop new strategies and grow stronger over time. Each time a major advancement occurs, either due to reaching a specific number of Experience Points or reaching a Milestone in the story, you will gain a Character Level.

For example, if you start at level 1 with 0 Experience Points and gain enough experience throughout a session to make your way to Level 2, you will mark this on your character sheet and upgrade your stats accordingly during your next Long Rest. Additionally, your DM may decide to use a Milestone system by granting you a level up upon reaching a new area or island, completing an important objective, or obtaining a key item or treasure.

Human
While many humans vary in shape and size, your human character will have these traits.

Ability Score Increase. One ability score of your choice increases by 2 and other ability scores increase by 1. Choosing different Human races replaces this ASI.

Age. Humans reach adulthood in their teens and live for around a century.

Alignment. There is no clear alignment that is consistent among all humans. Just about any alignment can be justified.

Size. Humans in the Jujutsu Kaisen world are typically 5-6 feet tall. Some can rest far outside this range, but your size will count as medium.

Speed. Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

Jujutsu Sorcerer
You are part of a family of sorcerers or have been involved from a young age, you gain the following:

Ability Score Increase. One ability score of your choice increases by 2 and another by 1.

Skills. You gain proficiency in martial weapons.

Trained Cursed Energy. You gain a Cursed Energy feat.
Superhuman
Very rarely, some humans may be astonishingly stronger than most others in the world, sometimes vastly stronger than the average human. If your human character happens to fall under this category, you can choose to replace the standard Human Ability Score Increase with these traits instead:

Ability Score Increase. You increase either your Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution score by 2 and the others by 1.

Natural Athlete. You have proficiency in the Athletics skill, if you already have proficiency, you instead gain Expertise.

Record Breaker. Your jumping distance is doubled.

Uncanny Endurance. You can focus on occasionally shrugging off injury. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to roll a d12. Add your Constitution modifier to the number rolled, and reduce the damage by that total. After you use this trait, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

Powerful Build. You count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.

Speed. Your movement speed is 35 feet.

Sorcerers who became cursed objects, and are now in a new body

Age. Your lifespan depends on the body you have possessed.

Alignment. Cursed vessels are almost always chaotic people, not caring about what happens to others around them and wanting to cause destruction.

Size. Your size depends on the race you have possessed.

Speed. Your base walking speed depends on the race you have possessed.

This Body Is Mine. You have advantage on saving throws against effects that would alter or change your form.

Languages. You can speak, read, and write Common and one other language of your choice.

Subrace. There are multiple forms of vessels, however they are all based on consuming cursed objects. There are the reincarnated, who were simply sorcerers who were consumed by creatures who were adapted for their incarnation. There are the death paintings, which take over the body of said vessel despite its host having a will. And then there are the incomplete and complete vessels. In case the cursed object's host still had a will, it would start as an incomplete vessel and then become a complete vessel after erasing the will of the old body owner.
Reincarnated
You are a sorcerer from a past era. Now you are in your second life through some deal or accident.

Ability Score Increase. You have been brought back to your peak, you can choose one ability score to increase by 2 and another ability score to increase by 2.

Life Experience. This isn't your first shot at life and last time you learned a few things. You will gain proficiency in two skills or one skill and one tool of your choice.

Cling to Life. You have died once and refuse to let it happen again. Whenever you are reduced to 0 hit points, you can choose to instead remain at 1 hit point, once per long rest.

Death Painting
A disastrous mixture of curse and man made by an evil scientist. Stuck as a fetus until fed to a host.

Ability Score Increase. Your cursed object has overcome the body of your initial host, so instead of gaining the host's ability scores, you gain a +3 to your Cursed Energy score. This cannot go above 20.

Durable Body. Once you incarnated into a vessel, due to your unnatural properties the body became more durable. Your maximum hit points increase by 2, and increase by 2 again every time you gain a level.

Poisonous Blood. Your birth came from someone from the Kamo clan, and from experimentation, your blood became poisonous. As a reaction, when you take piercing or slashing damage, you can choose a creature within 5 feet of you to take poison damage equal to your proficiency bonus. If the creature has an injury or less than their maximum hit points, they must make a DC 10 Constitution save or be poisoned until the end of their next turn.

Beings made of cursed energy within a shell, somehow gaining sentience.

Ability Score Improvement. You increase one ability score of your choice by 4, as you are purpose built for a single purpose.

Age. Your lifespan is hypothetically infinite if you repair yourself.

Alignment. Cursed Corpses are almost always neutral people, not caring about what happens to others around them and usually wanting to exist peacefully.

Size. Your size can be small to large.

Speed. Your base walking speed is 35 feet.

Unnatural. As a construct, you don’t need to breathe, drink, eat, or sleep. However you need materials to mend yourself during a rest.

Languages. You can speak, read, and write Common

Subrace. There are multiple forms of corpses. The soft bodies range from plush like, to normal living materials like flesh. Hard Shell is the hard skinned stone, wood, or metal.
Softbody
The simpler, more life-like Cursed Corpses are soft bodies, with their life-like design having both advantages and flaws.

Tailored Appearance. You gain expertise in either intimidation, persuasion, or performance.

Surprise. You can make a Performance check to disguise yourself as what you resemble. Your sudden reveal may stun an enemy. Once per long rest when you reveal yourself, you can force a creature within 10 feet to make a Wisdom saving throw:
(DC 10 + your proficiency bonus + your
Charisma modifier) becoming stunned until
the beginning of their turn on failure.

Hard Shell
The more complicated intricate form of Cursed Corpses are the hard shells. Their combat ability is not to be underestimated.

Integrated Armor. Your body has built-in defensive layers, which can be enhanced with armor.

  • You gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class.

  • You can don only armor with which you have proficiency. To don armor, you must incorporate it into your body over the course of 1 hour, during which you must remain in contact with the armor. To doff armor, you must spend 1 hour removing it. You can rest while donning or doffing armor in this way.

  • While you live, your armor can't be removed from your body against your will.

Beings made up of negative energy, festering over time.

Ability Score Improvement. You increase one ability score of your choice by 2 and another by 1.

Creature Type. You are Undead.

Age. You are cursed to live forever.

Alignment. Cursed Spirits rarely maintain any level of intelligence, but when they do, their alignment turns towards being more Chaotic or Evil.

Size. Your size can be Small or Medium.

Speed. Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

Spiritual Nature. You function completely differently from normal creatures:

  • You don’t need to eat, drink, breathe or sleep, but must remain inactive for 4 hours a day to gain the benefits of a long rest.

  • You have advantage on saving throws against disease and being poisoned, and you have resistance to poison damage.

  • You are immune to nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing.

  • You are invisible to creatures without cursed energy.

Cursed Energy Affinity. Due to your nature of being made of cursed energy, you are unable to utilize reverse cursed technique which is positive energy. Though you can still restore your body with pure cursed energy. Starting at 5th level, you can spend cursed energy up to your CE modifier to regain 5 hit points per cursed energy spent as an action once per turn.

Subrace. There are several types of cursed spirits, depending on your origin.

Vengeful
You were once human, but when you died your powerful grudge made you into a curse.

Grudge. When reduced to 0 hit points, you can choose to remain at 1 hit point. You can use this feature once per long rest.

Curse. When you choose this subrace, choose a race that you hated. You gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls against that race.

Imaginary
You are made up of humanity’s fears, formed from a shared negative image.

Frightful Presence. As an action, you can force all creatures within 30 feet of you to make a Wisdom saving throw against your Cursed Energy save DC. On a failure, they are frightened of you for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the save at the end of their turn. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.

Fearmonger. You gain proficiency in Intimidation and have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls against frightened creatures.

Disease
Plague and sickness are concepts cursed by humanity, giving rise to powerful curses.

Born from Plague. You are immune to disease and poison, as well as the poisoned condition. Your unarmed strikes deal 1d4 poison damage on a hit.

Walking Sickness. As an action, you can force all creatures within 30 feet of you to make a Constitution saving throw against your Cursed Energy save DC. On a failure, they gain the poisoned condition for 1 minute. A creature can repeat this save at the end of their turn. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you complete a long rest.

Cursed Womb
You are a young cursed spirit that has yet to develop.

Hard Shell. Your AC equals 14 + your Constitution modifier while not wearing armor.

Strong Constitution. Your hit point maximum increases by an amount equal to your level and increases by 1 whenever you gain a level.

Hit Points

Hit Dice: 1d12 per Juggernaut level
Hit Points at 1st Level: 12 + your Constitution modifier
Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d12 (or 7) + your Constitution modifier per Juggernaut level after 1st

Proficiencies

Armor: Light armor, medium armor, shields
Weapons: Simple weapons, martial weapons
Tools: None
Saving Throws: Strength, Constitution
Skills: Choose two from Animal Handling, Athletics, Intimidation, Nature, Perception, and Survival

Equipment

You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

  • (a) a greataxe or (b) any martial melee weapon

  • (a) two handaxes or (b) any simple weapon

  • An explorer's pack and four javelins

Innate Technique
Starting at 1st level, you were born with an Innate Technique. Innate Techniques are unique abilities congenitally engraved into the user's body, specifically in the right prefrontal cortex of the brain. Most jujutsu sorcerers are born with an innate technique that manifests around the age of five or six, which continually carves its formula into the user over time. You must choose one Innate Technique, all detailed under Innate Techniques. Your choice grants you features at 1st, and again at 3rd, 6th, 11th, and 18th level.
Combat Prowess
At 1st level, your life of scrapping and battling with beasts, has given you mastery of Combat styles that use unarmed strikes and Juggernaut weapons, which are melee weapons without the two-handed property, and improvised weapons. You can not use the finesse property of a weapon while using it as a Juggernaut weapon.

  • You can roll a d6 in place of the normal damage of your unarmed strike or Juggernaut weapon. This die changes as you gain Juggernaut levels, as shown in the scrapper column on the Juggernaut table.

  • When you use the Attack action with an unarmed strike or a Juggernaut weapon on your turn, you can make one unarmed strike or grapple as a bonus action. For example, if you take the Attack action and Attack with a Club, you can also make an Unarmed Strike or grapple as a Bonus Action, assuming you haven’t already taken a Bonus Action this turn.

Unarmored Defense
While you are not wearing any armor and not using a shield, your Armor Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Constitution modifier.

Focus
At 2nd level, in battle, you fight with an unstoppable focus. On your turn, you can enter a focus as a bonus action. While focused, you gain the following benefits while not wearing heavy armor:

  • You have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.

  • You have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.

  • You add your proficiency bonus to Strength based melee damage rolls.

Your focus lasts for 1 minute. It ends early if you are knocked unconscious. You can also end your focus on your turn as a bonus action. You can focus a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus each long rest.
Reckless Blows
Starting at 2nd level, you can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with fierce desperation. When you make your first attack on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you advantage on melee weapon attack rolls using Strength during this turn, but attack rolls against you have advantage until your next turn.

Ability Score Improvement
When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. You can also ignore this increase to instead gain a Feat.

Extra Attack
Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

Pursuer
Starting at 5th level, as part of your bonus action while entering a focus, you can move up to half your movement speed towards an enemy.

Honed Instincts
By 7th level, your instincts are so honed that you have advantage on initiative rolls.

Additionally, if you are surprised at the beginning of combat and aren't incapacitated, you can act normally on your first turn, but only if you enter your focus before doing anything else on that turn.

Brutal Blows
Beginning at 9th level, you can roll one additional weapon damage die when determining the extra damage for a critical hit with a melee attack.

This increases to two additional dice at 13th level and three additional dice at 17th level.
Lock In
Starting at 10th level, your focus can keep you fighting despite grievous wounds. If you drop to 0 hit points while you're focused and don't die outright, you can make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw. If you succeed, you drop to 1 hit point instead.

Each time you use this feature after the first, the DC increases by 5. When you finish a short or long rest, the DC resets to 10.

Curse Resistance
Beginning at 14th level, you also gain resistance to necrotic damage while focused.

Endless Focus
Beginning at 15th level, your focus is so fierce that it only ends if you fall unconscious or if you choose to end it.

Unstoppable
At 20th level, you are aware of your role in society and will do your best to fulfill it. Your Strength and Constitution scores increase by 4. Your maximum for those scores is now 24.

Hit Points

Hit Dice: 1d8 per scout level
Hit Points at 1st Level: 8 + your Constitution modifier
Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d8 (or 5) + your Constitution modifier per scout level after 1st

Proficiencies

Armor: Light armor
Weapons: Simple weapons, handguns, longswords, rapiers, and shortswords
Tools: None
Saving Throws: Dexterity, Wisdom
Skills: Choose three skills from Acrobatics, Animal Handling, Athletics, History, Insight, Intimidation, Perception, and Survival

Equipment

  • (a) a rapier or (b) a shortsword

  • (a) a shortbow and quiver of 20 arrows or (b) a shortsword

  • (a) a burglar's pack, (b) dungeoneer's pack, or (c) an explorer's pack

  • Dense coat, two daggers, and thieves' tools

Innate Technique
Starting at 1st level, you were born with an Innate Technique. Innate Techniques are unique abilities congenitally engraved into the user's body, specifically in the right prefrontal cortex of the brain. Most jujutsu sorcerers are born with an innate technique that manifests around the age of five or six, which continually carves its formula into the user over time. You must choose one Innate Technique, all detailed under Innate Techniques. Your choice grants you features at 1st, and again at 3rd, 6th, 11th, and 18th level.

Quick Strikes
At 1st level, your practice of martial arts gives you mastery of combat styles that use unarmed strikes and scout weapons, which are shortswords and any simple melee weapons that don't have two-handed or heavy properties.

You gain the following benefits:

  • You can use Dexterity instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of your unarmed strikes and scout weapons.

  • You can roll a d4 in place of the normal damage of your unarmed strike or scout weapon. This die changes as you gain scout levels, as shown in the damage dice column of the Scout table.

  • When you use the Attack action with an unarmed strike or a scout weapon on your turn, you can make one unarmed strike as a bonus action. For example, if you take the Attack action and attack with a quarterstaff, you can also make an unarmed strike as a bonus action, assuming you haven't already taken a bonus action this turn.

Unparalleled Movement
At 1st level, your speed increases by 10 feet. This bonus increases when you reach certain scout levels, as shown in the scout table
At 9th level, you gain the ability to move along vertical surfaces and across liquids on your turn without falling during the move.

Swift Movement
Starting at 2nd level, your quick thinking and agility allow you to move and act quickly. You can take the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action as a bonus action.

Sharp Eyes
At 2nd level, you can make a bonus action Insight check against your opponents against an opponent’s Deception check. On a success, you gain an advantage on all rolls against that opponent for that turn.

Ability Score Improvement
When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. You can also ignore this increase to instead gain a Feat.

Eagle Eyes
Starting at 5th level, you can see even fine details up to a mile away. You also gain advantage on Perception checks using sight.

Extra Attack
At 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once when you use the Attack action during your turn.

Evasion
Beginning at 7th level, you can nimbly dodge out of the way of certain area effects, such as a red dragon's fiery breath or an Ice Storm technique. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail. At 15th level, you can choose a second saving throw and gain the same effects from it.
Tactical Retreat
At 10th level, if an opponent moves within 5ft of you, you can move up to your movement speed as a reaction.
When you reach 15th level, you can move up to twice your speed.

Scanning Eyes
Beginning at 13th level, you can now as a part of Sharp Eyes tell your opponent's weaknesses(Weak Points, Vulnerabilities) and main attacks (Damage Type and highest damage action).

Sixth Sense
Beginning at 14th level, you gain advantage on Dexterity saving throws and blindsight out to 30 feet.

Swift Dodge
Starting at 17th level, when an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to ignore the attack's damage against you. You can use this feature a number of times equal to half your proficiency bonus (rounded up) per long rest.

Unfathomable Speed
Beginning at 20th level, your speed is faster than anyone can track. Your movement becomes instant and cannot provoke opportunity attacks.

Hit Points

Hit Dice: 1d6 per strategist level
Hit Points at 1st Level: 6 + your Constitution modifier
Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d6 (or 4) + your Constitution modifier per strategist level after 1st

Proficiencies

Armor: None

Weapons: Daggers, darts, slings, quarterstaffs, and handguns

Tools: None

Saving Throws: Intelligence, Wisdom

Skills: Choose two from Arcana, History, Insight, Investigation, Medicine, and Religion

Equipment

  • (a) a handgun or (b) a dagger

  • (a) a component pouch or (b) an arcane focus

  • (a) a scholar's pack or (b) an explorer's pack

  • A technique manual

Innate Technique
Starting at 1st level, you were born with an Innate Technique. Innate Techniques are unique abilities congenitally engraved into the user's body, specifically in the right prefrontal cortex of the brain. Most jujutsu sorcerers are born with an innate technique that manifests around the age of five or six, which continually carves its formula into the user over time. You must choose one Innate Technique, all detailed under Innate Techniques. Your choice grants you features at 1st, and again at 3rd, 6th, 11th, and 18th levels.

Quick Recovery
You have a pool of latent cursed energy that replenishes when you take a long rest. The pool equals half your Strategist level (rounded up) and you can draw from it at will.
For example, if you're a 4th-level strategist, you have a pool of 2 cursed energy points. You can recover either 1 at two different times or 2 at once.

Technique Creativity
At 2nd level, you gain the ability to twist cursed techniques to suit your needs. You gain two of the following Modification options of your choice. You gain another one at 10th and 17th levels.
You can use only one Modification option on a technique when you cast it unless otherwise specified.

  • Careful Technique. When you cast a technique that forces other creatures to make a saving throw, you can protect some of those creatures from the technique's full force. To do so, you spend 1 cursed energy and choose a number of those creatures up to your Cursed Energy modifier (minimum of one). A chosen creature automatically succeeds on its saving throw against the technique.

  • Distant Technique. When you cast a technique that has a range of 5 feet or greater, you can spend 1 cursed energy to double the range of the technique. When you cast a technique that has a range of touch, you can spend 1 cursed energy to make the range of the technique 30 feet.

  • Empowered Technique. When you roll damage for a technique, you can spend 1 cursed energy to reroll a number of the damage dice up to your Cursed Energy modifier (minimum of one). You must use the new rolls. You can use Empowered technique even if you have already used a different Modification option.

  • Extended Technique. When you cast a technique that has a duration of 1 minute or longer, you can spend 1 cursed energy to double its duration, to a maximum duration of 24 hours.

  • Heightened Technique. When you cast a technique that forces a creature to make a saving throw to resist its effects, you can spend 3 cursed energy to give one target of the technique disadvantage on its first saving throw against the technique.

  • Quickened Technique. When you cast a technique that has a casting time of 1 action, you can spend 2 cursed energy to change the casting time to 1 bonus action for this casting.

  • Seeking Technique. If you make an attack roll for a technique and miss, you can spend 2 cursed energy to reroll the d20, and you must use the new roll. You can use Seeking technique even if you have already used a different Modification option.

  • Subtle Technique. When you cast a technique, you can spend 1 cursed energy to cast it without somatic or verbal components.

  • Transmuted Technique. When you cast a technique that deals a type of damage from the following list, you can spend 1 cursed energy to change that damage type to one of the other listed types: acid, cold, fire, lightning, poison, or thunder.

  • Twinned Technique. When you cast a technique that targets only one creature and doesn't have a range of self, you can spend a number of cursed energy equal to the technique's cost to target a second creature in range with the same technique (1 cursed energy if the technique is free). To be eligible, a technique must be incapable of targeting more than one creature at the technique's current level.

Signature Move

Starting at 3rd level you can reinforce your barriers with cursed energy. You can spend additional cursed energy up to your Cursed Energy modifier to give your Dark Cube a reinforcement for every cursed energy spent:
Persistence. Your Cube gains 10 additional hit points for every 1 reinforcement, +1 bonus to AC for every 2 reinforcements and lasts an additional minute for every 3 reinforcements.
Toughness. Your Cube reduces all damage taken by 1 for each reinforcement.
Size. For every 2 reinforcements, you can make your Dark Cube 5 feet larger, allowing you to fit more creatures. (10 ft < 15 ft < 20ft)
At 11th level, you can spend up to twice your CE modifier on reinforcements.

Perfect Cube
At 6th level, you have learned to create a nearly indestructible Dark Cube. For an additional 5 CE, you can create a Perfect Cube (this cursed energy counts towards the Cube’s Reinforcements).
Your Perfect Cube has resistance to all damage and ignores features or abilities that deal higher damage against objects and structures or would destroy, see into, or invade your barrier.

Maximum: Midnight Armor
At 11th level, you have learned to manifest your barrier around yourself. You can spend 6 cursed energy as an action to manifest parts of your cube around your body like armor for 1 minute or until the armor is destroyed:

  • You gain the hit points of your barrier as temporary hit points.

  • Your AC equals your Dark Cube’s AC.

  • Your unarmed strikes can use your CE modifier for attack rolls and deal 3d8 + CE modifier necrotic damage on a hit.

  • You can spend additional cursed energy up to twice your cursed energy modifier to also gain the benefits of any reinforcement other than Size.

Domain Expansion: Primordial Gap
At 18th level you have mastered your technique, allowing you to expand your domain. In your domain all of your Dark Cubes automatically count as Perfect Cubes. At initiative 20, you create 3 Perfect Cubes, potentially trapping 3 creatures within your domain inside Perfect Cubes. They are treated as having Reinforcements up to your CE modifier. These cubes disappear when your domain ends.

Through your beliefs, you set both your weapon and heart alight with your blazing courage.

Cursed Energy
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

Ignition
Starting at 1st level, your technique allows yourself to ignite your weapon in flames, increasing your fire power. You can spend up to your proficiency bonus as a bonus action while holding a melee weapon, igniting said weapon in flames for 1 minute. For the duration, the weapon deals an additional 1d6 fire damage on a hit per CE spent, and emits bright light for 5 feet and dim light for another 10 feet.
This increases to 1d8 per ce spent at 6th level and again to 1d10 at 11th level and 1d12 at 18th level.

                     **Mantle of Courage**

Starting at 3rd level, you can strengthen both yourself and your weapon. When you use Ignition, you ignore any detriments or penalties of the weapon or can use it on yourself for your unarmed strikes, potentially recreating a lost limb for the duration.
While Ignition is active, you can spend 3 CE as a free action on your turn. You emit an aura of flames within 10 feet of you for 1 minute, giving you resistance to fire and cold damage. An enemy that enters your mantle or starts their turn there must make a Constitution saving throw, taking your Ignition damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful save.
Eternal Flames
At 6th level, when you spend at least 3 ce on Ignition, you can increase the weapon’s range by 10 feet, ignore resistance to fire damage and when you miss with a weapon attack by 2 or less, you deal half your Ignition damage.
This increases to 3 or less at 11th level and 4 or less at 18th level.

Maximum: Conflagration
At 11th level, while your technique may be simple, that does not mean it isn’t powerful. While holding a melee weapon you can spend 10 ce as an action to swing your weapon, creating a 30 feet cone of intense flame and heat. All creatures within range must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 10d12 fire damage and being knocked prone on a failed save or half as much on a successful save.
If a creature fails by 5 or more, they gain severe burns and take additional fire damage equal to your proficiency bonus from any source of fire damage until they finish a long rest.

Domain Expansion: Fire of the Heart
Finally at 18th level you have learned to expand your domain. Any melee weapon you are holding is treated as having the maximum cursed energy used for Ignition and is imbued with your domain’s guaranteed hit. At initiative 20, all creatures of your choice within your domain suffer the damage of your Mantle of Courage.

You were born with a complex ability held and practiced by the Kamo family, you can control your blood.

Cursed Energy
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.
You regain all spent cursed energy on a long rest.

Blood Constructs
Starting at 1st level, you have been blessed with the Innate Technique of the Kamo clan, making you begin with the most basic technique, the blood constructs. You can pull blood from an available source to create a semi-solid construct. As an action for 1 CE and 1 HP, you can create a small construct smaller than a 5ft by 5ft space. For every 5 ft the price increases by 1 CE and HP. You can ignore the HP cost if you have an alternate source of blood. These constructs have HP equal to your level times CE spent.
Once as part of a long rest, you can spend $100 and hit points up to your proficiency bonus to fill a Blood Bag with your own blood. This Blood Bag counts as a source of hit points for your Blood Manipulation features. A Blood Bag lasts 5 days outside of refrigeration before it goes bad. You can have a number of Blood Bags equal to your Constitution modifier at once.

Blood Techniques
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your blood in a manner fit for battle. When you use a Blood Manipulation feature, you can ignore the HP cost if you have an alternate source of blood. You gain three of following techniques and gain an additional two at 6th and 11th level:

  • Crimson Binding: As an action for 1 CE and 1 HP, you unleash a red blood net, forcing a target Large or smaller within 30ft to make a Strength saving throw or be restrained. They can repeat the save at the start of their turn.

  • Slicing Exorcism: As an action for 1 CE and 1 HP you spin a ring of blood and unleash it as a projectile. Make a ranged CE attack against a target within 60 ft, on a hit you deal 1d10 + CE modifier necrotic damage. If used with Convergence, the attack still deals your CE modifier on a miss of 5 or less.

  • Blood Edge: You can spend CE up to your Cursed Energy modifier to create a melee weapon as a free action which counts as magical for overcoming resistances. For every two Cursed Energy used the weapon gains an additional damage tier(d10->d12->2d8) and lasts 1 minute. If used with Convergence, it only gains the benefit of the damage tier increase.

  • Crimson Rain: As an action for 3 CE and 2 HP, you pick an area within 60 ft, that spot becomes the center of a 15 ft radius of a rain of blood spikes. All creatures in that radius must make a Dexterity Saving throw taking 3d10 piercing damage on failure or half as much on a success. If used with Convergence, a target is also knocked prone on a failed save.

  • Blood Burst: For 1 CE and 1 HP upon hitting with a weapon attack once per turn, you cover your strike with blood, causing it to explode on impact. The creature must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure they take 4d6 necrotic damage.

  • Blood Meteorite: As an action for 1 CE and 3 HP you create a solid crystal of blood launched like an asteroid. You can make a ranged CE attack against a target in 30 ft. On a hit, this attack deals 4d4 + CE modifier in bludgeoning damage.

  • Blood Geyser: As an action for 3 CE and 3 HP, you can choose a 5 feet space within 10 ft of yourself and saturate it with blood. When a creature starts their turn there or enters that area, all creatures within 5 feet must make a Dexterity saving throw or take 5d10 bludgeoning damage and get launched 30ft in the air or half as much on a success.

Flowing Red Scale
At 3rd level, you can control body temperature, pulse rate, and the number of red blood cells to give yourself greatly increased physical capabilities. You can spend 3 Cursed Energy as a bonus action to gain the following benefits for 1 minute:

  • Your walking speed is doubled

  • You gain a +2 bonus to your AC

  • You advantage on Dexterity saving throws and Strength checks

  • You gain an additional action on each of your turns. That action can be used only to take the Attack (one weapon attack only), Dash, Disengage, Hide, or Use an Object action.

Convergence
At 6th level, you compress and condense blood to its absolute limit. Before you use a blood manipulation technique with a casting time of one action, you can spend your bonus action, reaction and movement to enhance the technique's potency, gaining the following benefits:

  • You deal additional damage die equal to your proficiency bonus

  • Your damage die increases by 1 level(d10->d12->2d8)

  • The range increases by 30 feet

If you spend an additional turn using your action, bonus action, reaction and movement to charge up Convergence before using your technique, you gain these benefits an additional time and gain advantage on the first technique attack roll or can force creatures to make their first saving throw against your technique at disadvantage. Certain Blood Techniques may have additional or different bonuses if used with Convergence that are listed with each technique.

Alternatively, instead of spending time to compress blood, you quicken the process with cursed energy. You can spend 1 additional CE when using a Blood Technique to gain additional benefits. Slicing Exorcism, Blood Burst and Blood Meteorite deal 1 additional damage dice on a hit. Crimson Binding increases the DC by 1. Crimson Rain and Blood Geyser deal 1 additional damage per damage dice.
At 11th level, the additional CE you can spend increases to 2, which causes these bonuses to double if spending 2 instead of 1. At 18th level, this becomes 3 CE, which can cause these bonuses to triple. You cannot use both methods of Convergence on the same technique.

Piercing Blood
Beginning at 11th level, you can compress your blood into a deadly supersonic beam. As an action for 8 CE and 5 HP, you unleash a 100ft line of blood. Creatures in range must make a Dexterity save taking 10d8 piercing on a failure.
If used with Convergence, you can continue shooting the beam for an additional round. Any creature that enters the lingering Piercing Blood must make the saving throw. As an action you can swing the line, making it into a 130 feet cone forcing an additional Dexterity save and the technique ends.

Domain Expansion: Bloodbath
When you reach 18th level, you gain your domain expansion. At Initiative 20, all creatures take 4d12 necrotic damage as their blood attacks them from the inside. While in the domain your blood manipulation techniques can use hit points from other creatures within the domain.

You were born with a simple although tricky ability to swap places with your opponents with a clap.

Cursed Energy
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.
You regain all spent cursed energy on a long rest.

Boogie
At 1st level, you have created a unique technique to switch places with your others, extremely simple yet effective. You can switch places with a willing creature or magical object within 30 feet of you by clapping for 1 Cursed Energy. You can use this technique as an action or bonus action, or you can also swap as a reaction for 2 additional Cursed Energy.

Woogie
Starting at 3rd level, you have extended the grasp of your technique as well as its versatility. Your Boogie gains the following bonuses:

  • Unwilling creatures can be switched

  • You can make two creatures other than yourself swap places

  • Enemies teleported are disorientated and lose their reaction

Clap Back
Beginning at 6th level, “The act of applause is an acclamation of the soul”, you have gained a deeper understanding of your technique and how it can be used, your Boogie gains the following benefits:

  • Your range increases to 45 feet.

  • The Cursed Energy cost is reduced by 1 Cursed Energy for all Boogie Woogie techniques (min cost of 1).

  • You can use Boogie once per turn as a free action for 1 cursed energy.

Round of Applause
When you reach 11th level, you have understood the true depths of Boogie Woogie, your Boogie gains the following:

  • Your range increases to 60 feet

  • When you switch places with an ally who was previously in melee range of an enemy right before the switch, your next attack roll has advantage, the same goes if you teleport an enemy into range or an ally into range.

  • You can use Boogie on up to four creatures at once.

Domain Expansion: Standing Ovation
Reaching 18th level, you have mastered the beat of Boogie Woogie, you gain your domain expansion. Within your domain, you can use Boogie as a free action an unlimited number of times on your turn (not limited to once per turn) without spending CE.

You were born with the horrifying but useful ability to swap bodies and take the abilities from that body.

Cursed Energy
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.
You regain all spent cursed energy on a long rest.

Graverobber
Starting at 1st level, you have a rather disgusting technique, which is frowned upon by the majority of sorcerers. When you have a humanoid creature's corpse, you can spend 1 cursed energy during a long rest to put your brain on that creature through a transfer technique. While on the creature's body, you lose any racial features of your old body but keep all of your class features. You gain the following benefits while inside the body:

  • The creature’s innate technique features are now yours.

  • The creature’s cursed energy features are now yours.

  • The creature's racial features are now yours.

  • The creature's ability scores overwrite yours but you keep your Charisma, Wisdom, and Intelligence scores.

  • The creature's proficiencies and languages are now yours.

When you change into that creature's body, it will look the same outside of having a scar on its forehead, which is a sign your brain is inside its body. You can pull the top of your head to show your brain, which is a normal brain with a human mouth. Other creatures can try to identify you're not the humanoid by making a DC 30 Insight check. Creatures who knew the body's owner before you stole it can do the roll with advantage.
Skill Theft
Beginning at 3rd, your control over the body you take over increases. You can choose to take two of the body’s Innate Technique features. Cursed Energy features, or proficiencies from a body you have inhabited in the past. You cannot use Innate Technique features from different techniques at the same time. If you do, one of them deactivates until you are only using one innate technique. You can choose two more features at 6th, 11th, and 18th levels.

Immortality
At the 18th level, your age is the same as the body you take over, making you immortal as long as you keep switching bodies.

Your technique summons a centipede shikigami to fight with you.

Cursed Energy
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

Cursed Centipede
Starting at 1st level, you can summon your shikigami as a bonus action. You can command your shikigami on your turn as a bonus action. Your centipede can enter your space, floating around you as a shroud providing the following benefits:

  • On a hit with a melee attack, you deal an additional 1d10 damage as your Centipede fights with you.

  • You gain a bonus to AC equal to your proficiency bonus.

  • You can make an additional melee attack as a bonus action.

  • When you or the centipede take damage, you can choose to have the other take the damage instead. If this damage would reduce the centipede to 0 hit points, you take the remaining damage.

You can summon your shikigami for free once per long rest and again for 3 CE. You can only have one Cursed Centipede summoned at a time. The centipede cannot be targeted with attacks directly while acting as a Shroud. However, if you are reduced to 0 HP, any remaining damage affects the shikigami.

Insect Storage
Starting at 3rd level, you can store items in the stomach of your centipede. You must have your centipede summoned to take items in or out of it and items can be no larger than a shield or polearm. Your centipede can store a number of pounds equal to twice your Cursed Energy score times your proficiency bonus and you can store or withdraw an item as an object interaction. If you die, the items stored in your centipede explode from your stomach.
Earthquake
Starting at 6th level, as an action you can spend 3 CE to force all creatures within 30 feet to make a Strength saving throw if they are on the ground. On a failure, they take 6d6 bludgeoning damage and fall prone. On a success, they take half as much damage. If your cursed centipede is summoned, you can instead do this as a bonus action. This damage increases to 10d6 at 11th and 14d6 at 18th level.

Additionally, you gain 5 stat points you can spend to increase your centipede’s ability scores (max of 22). You can now add your proficiency bonus to any saving throw or skill check it makes.
You gain 5 additional stat points at 11th level.

Hundred Leg Catastrophe
At 11th level, your technique increases by leaps and bounds. As an action for 8 cursed energy, you can launch up to 3 giant centipedes at targets within 120 feet, making a ranged cursed energy attack roll for each. On a hit, they deal 8d10 necrotic damage and the target must make a Strength saving throw. On a failure, the target is pushed or pulled 30ft closer or further (your choice) and falls prone.
Additionally, you can now have two cursed centipedes summoned at a time. While you have two cursed centipedes acting as your shroud, you can make 2 melee attacks as a bonus action and instead add 3 + your proficiency bonus to your AC.

Domain Expansion: Oomukade Banzai
At 18th level, you have mastered your technique allowing you to open your domain. Within your domain, your cursed centipedes’s attacks are guaranteed hits. At initiative 20, all creatures are restrained by cursed centipedes and can make a Strength (Athletics) check at the beginning of their turns to escape. The centipedes restraining a creature assists all attacks against the target, causing such attacks to deal an additional 2d10 damage. The cursed centipedes disappear once the domain ends or the creature is no longer grappled.

Your technique allows you to create perfect clones of yourself.

Cursed Energy
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

One Man Army
Starting at 1st level, you can spend 3 CE as an action to create a clone within 5 feet of yourself for 8 hours. They are completely indistinguishable from you in every way. A clone has 1/4 of your hit point maximum (rounded up) as well as your AC and access to all your class features and cursed techniques, but not innate technique features. Any cursed energy or features used is treated as if you spent it. Your Clones act on your turn, but can only make one attack on their turn even if you have Extra Attack or bonus action attacks. You can replace any of your attacks on your turn with an attack from the Clone’s space. Your Clones do not have any of your items.
You can have a number of clones equal to your proficiency bonus at once and when a clone dies, the number of clones you can have is reduced by 1 for 1 minute.

Twice the Fun
At 3rd level, you can now create multiple clones as an action by spending 3 CE for each clone. When you make a melee attack against a creature while a Clone is within 5 feet of the target, you gain advantage on the attack roll.

Three is a Crowd
At 6th level you have become more skillful and efficient with the creation of your clones. Your Clones now have 1/2 of your total hit points. When one of your Clones is reduced to 0 hit points, you regain 1 cursed energy.

Four is a Party
At 11th level, you have mastered the ability to choose which of your Clones is your actual body. Your Clones have hit points equal to yours and you can swap bodies with one of your clones as a bonus action for 1 CE, trading hit points and causing that Clone to become your new body. When you are reduced to 0 hit points or killed outright while you have a Clone active, you can instead transfer yourself into one of your clones, gaining the Clone’s current hit points.

Your Clones can now create one Clone by spending your Cursed Energy with each Clone counting against your limit.

Domain Expansion: Divide and Conquer
Finally at 18th level you have perfected your technique, allowing you to expand your domain. You can now create one Clone as a bonus action without spending cursed energy once per turn (Your Clones do not gain this benefit). Within your domain, you can have an unlimited number of Clones. Your Clone’s attacks are guaranteed hits within your domain.
At initiative 20, an additional clone appears. All Clones created with your domain disappear when the domain ends.

Why do you need an explanation? How about a joke!

Cursed Energy
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

Comedy
Beginning at 1st level, reality bends around you to fit your idea of comedy. As an action for 1 cursed energy, you activate your technique for 1 minute while maintaining concentration. When you are damaged, you can spend 1 cursed energy to take no damage as some funny phenomena allows you to avoid damage (Eg. you open an umbrella to block an attack, you slip on a banana peel to dodge, etc). You also gain proficiency in Performance and at 11th level you gain Expertise.

A creature that knows how your technique works can make a contested Charisma (Persuasion) or Wisdom (Insight) check as an action to deconstruct your humor against your Charisma (Performance). If they roll higher, your technique deactivates as you lose confidence in your comedy and cannot use your technique. You can make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw at the end of your turn to regain control of your technique and cause it to reactivate as normal.
Commit to the Bit
At 3rd level, you have learned to use your comedy to supplement your abilities. You gain access to the following gags while your technique is active:

Blasting Off. On a hit with a melee attack, you can spend 1 CE to cause the target to go flying up to 60 ft away from you and fall prone. This increases to 90 ft at 6th level, 120 ft at 11th level, and 200 ft at 18th level.
Props. As a bonus action for 2 CE, you create a number of items equal to your CE modifier that fit in a 5 ft cube that help with your current joke or bit. These items increase to a 10 ft cube at 6th level, 15 ft cube at 11th level, and 20 ft cube at 18th level. These props last for 1 minute or until your technique deactivates.
Powerful Punchline. As an action for 3 CE, you let loose a good punchline related to a joke you tell or a bit you have going. Choose a range and source of the punchline:

  • 30 ft diameter sphere within 80 ft

  • 60 ft long, 5 ft wide line

  • 30 ft cone

All creatures within range must make a Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution saving throw based on the source of the punchline. On a failed save, a target takes your proficiency bonus + your CE modifier in d8s of bludgeoning, piercing, slashing, or psychic damage and an additional effect depending on the punchline (Eg. A bus runs someone over. Creatures in a 60 ft long, 5 ft wide line must make a Dexterity saving throw or take 5d8 bludgeoning damage and are pushed to the end of the line and knocked prone on a failed save or half as much damage and not pushed or prone on a success). This damage cannot kill a person since comedy isn’t funny if someone dies.

Comedic Foil
At 6th level, you can even hijack the thoughts of others to go along with your jokes and skits. They find themselves saying things that lead into your jokes. A creature that starts their turn within 300 ft of you while your technique is active must make a Cursed Energy saving throw. On a failure, they cannot use any cursed techniques that would interfere with your current joke until their next turn.

Additionally, you can choose to not allow other creatures to interfere with your combat while your technique is active. This stops other creatures from rolling for initiative or affecting the battle in any way as some random reason prevents them from joining in. You can also choose to remove a creature’s ability to sense cursed energy while they are within 300 ft of you while your technique is active to stop them from being distracted from your jokes.

Maximum: Peak Comedy
At 11th level, you can activate your technique at maximum efficiency. As an action for 10 cursed energy, you activate Comedy for 1 minute. During this minute you gain the following improvements:

  • Once per turn you can use your Gags without spending cursed energy. You can use Comedy’s negation for free a number of times equal to your CE modifier each round.

  • The number of props you can create becomes twice your CE modifier. This becomes thrice your CE modifier at 18th level.

  • The range and radius of your Powerful Punchline are doubled and you can spend 2 cursed energy to deal additional damage dice equal to your proficiency bonus.

  • As an action you completely change the scene and scenario into one fitting of the joke you tell, teleporting creatures within 100ft into a cutaway. A target in the cutaway must make a Wisdom save or cannot attack unless they make it fit into the cutaway gag.

Domain Expansion: Stand Up Comedy
At 18th level, you have finally learned to expand your domain. At initiative 20, you can force a cutaway. Completely changing the scene and scenario into one fitting of the joke you are telling. A creature within your domain cannot attack you unless they can make it fit into the cutaway gag. If a creature does not act according to your jokes and gags, the audience boos them and they take 8d8 psychic damage. A creature can only take this damage once per round.
As a Full Turn Action (Action + Bonus Action + Movement) while within your domain, you can tell a joke and make a Charisma (Persuasion) check. All creatures within your domain can make a Wisdom (Insight) check to criticize or attack it. A creature that chooses not to roll or rolls lower than you takes 8d8 psychic damage.

Construction, as the name implies, allows the user to conjure objects from nothing.

Cursed Energy
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.
You regain all spent cursed energy on a long rest.

Construct
Beginning at 1st, you can create any kind of object you understand with your technique, although without much efficiency. As a bonus action for 3 CE, you create one non-magical weapon OR simple object that fits in a 3 ft cube in your hand or within 5 ft of you, as long as you have basic understanding and information of its properties.

You can spend additional CE to create an object with one additional object’s properties or increase the cube by 1 ft. (Eg. You create a greatsword mixed with a spear with both the Heavy, two-handed, and the Versatile and Thrown (20/60) properties. When mixing a light and heavy weapon, choose which property it will maintain.)

Cursed Creation
At 3rd level, your construction technique has improved by a lot, you can now even create cursed objects. You can create a generic imbued Cursed Tool or a specific technique cursed tool you have seen for 3 cursed energy + 2 for every grade it has above 4. These cursed tools last a number of hours equal to your Cursed Energy modifier, before disappearing.
You can make a Special Grade (Legendary) Cursed Tool. However, due to the backlash of your technique, you will die afterward. You cannot be revived in any way, shape or form after using this feature.
Liquid Metal
At 6th level, you have learned how to create liquid metal, a substance with fluid form and changeable volume but stable physical properties due to semi-autonomous cursed energy. As part of creating a weapon with your construction, you can spend up to an additional 4 cursed energy to make them become fluid with volume for 1 minute. This allows you to extend the range of melee weapons 10ft per cursed energy.

In addition, whenever you attack with them in this increased range form their damage die tier will increase by 1 per additional cursed energy used. (1d8->1d10->1d12->2d6->2d8)

Insectoid Armor
At 11th level, you realize you need a way to efficiently use your cursed energy despite being an inefficient technique. You have learned how to create armor that simulates the efficiency of an insect's bug body. As a bonus action for 10 cursed energy, you can surround yourself in this armor and gain the following benefits for 1 hour:

  • Your Strength, Dexterity, and Armor Class scores increase by +4, as a result of the efficiency of the constructs.

  • You will gain resistance to non-magical bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage. This becomes immunity at 18th level.

  • Wings will sprout from your back, granting you a flying speed equal to your walking speed. In addition, you can now use a free action to dash on your turn.

  • Your unarmed strikes deal two additional damage dice and your unarmed strikes roll one additional damage dice on a critical.

Domain Expansion: Threefold Affliction
Finally at 18th level, you have refined your technique to the maximum point, now gaining your domain expansion. While inside your domain, you can now create any of your items by spending no cursed energy. All of these items will deal two additional damage dice and attacks made with them cannot miss. However, these weapons will only last until the end of the domain.

You can recreate the subject of contracts you find, like receipts.

Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

Recreation
Starting at 1st level, you have learned the basics of your technique in materializing things from receipts, paying the cost in cursed energy. You start with 5 receipts of your choice. To materialize from a receipt, you spend the required cursed energy as an action. The receipt then becomes ashes and you cannot use this technique if the receipts are wet. You can summon materializations within 100 ft.

Size CE Cost
Tiny 2
Small 4

Large 8

Gargantuan 20

Object. You summon an object from the receipt, spending cursed energy equal to its size.
Vehicle. You can summon a vehicle from the receipt, spending cursed energy equal to its size.
Reservation. You can use a reservation receipt for 4 cursed energy, giving you the same effects staying on said place for all of the duration would. For example, a 2 day spa reservation would give you the benefits of a long rest.
Structure. You can create a structure from a receipt for 20 CE.

If you create an object over a creature, they must make a Dexterity save against your CE save DC. On a failure they take 2d6 bludgeoning damage for every size larger than Tiny the object is. If the object is Huge or larger, a creature takes half as much damage on a successful save or is knocked prone and restrained under the object in addition to damage on a fail. Anything created through your technique lasts indefinitely.
Quick Spender
At 3rd level, you become better in using your technique with faster activation. You can now materialize receipts as an action or bonus action. At 18th level, you can materialize receipts as an action, bonus action or free action on your turn.

Splurge
At 6th level, you become even better with your technique and can use multiple receipts at a time. You can now use a number of receipts at once equal to your proficiency bonus, as long as you're holding them.

Contractual Control
At 11th level, you have learned how to manipulate your materializations using your mind. You can manipulate objects or vehicles as a bonus action by spending 3 cursed energy per object or vehicle manipulated. Anything you use this on disappears afterwards.
Objects. You can manipulate a number of objects you have summoned telepathically. You can move them in the air up to 60 ft, and can use them normally from afar.
Weapon. Once per turn when you take the attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with a melee cursed energy attack roll with said object if it was a weapon. On a hit, it deals 5 of the weapon's damage dice. This increases to 7 dice at 15th level and 10 at 18th level.
Vehicles. You can order a vehicle to ride up to 60 ft. A creature in the path must make a Dexterity save or take the vehicle damage dice (depending on size) and be knocked prone.

Domain Expansion: Black Friday
At 18th level, you have learned to expand your domain. You can use Recreation and Contractual Control at no cursed energy cost within your domain. At initiative 20, you gain a random receipt. D4 (1: Object, 2: Vehicles, 3: Reservation, 4: Structure) The DM decides the nature of the receipt.

Cursed Cannon, as the name says, allows you to unleash blasts of cursed energy. As simple as it is, its power is undeniable.

Cursed Energy
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being Charisma or Wisdom.
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + CE modifier + proficiency bonus.
You regain all spent cursed energy on a long rest.

Granite Blast
Starting at 1st level, your CE output is off the charts, and thanks to your technique allowing you to output it in a destructive death ray. As an action, you can spend 1 cursed energy to release a beam. Make a ranged cursed energy attack roll with a range of 150/600 feet. On a hit, it deals 2d6 + your CE modifier in necrotic damage. Before you make your attack roll, you can spend additional cursed energy up to your CE modifier to deal one additional damage dice per CE spent.

Beginning at 3rd level, the damage increases to 3d6, to 4d8 at 6th, to 5d10 at 11th, to 6d12 at 18th level.

Grape Choux
At 3rd level, your versatility with your blasts has increased. For 1 additional cursed energy, you can split your Granite Blast into different blasts, with damage dice spread evenly between them. Only two of the damage rolls can add your Cursed Energy modifier to the damage roll.
Dessert Deluge
Beginning at 6th level, your shots are malleable and extremely difficult to avoid. Once per attack roll, you can choose to spend up to 5 cursed energy points to add to the attack roll.

Maximum: Granita Lusso
At 11th level, your output reaches an all time high. As an action for 6 cursed energy, all creatures in a 10 ft wide 60 ft long line must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they take twice your Granite Blast damage or half as much on a success. You can spend additional cursed energy up to your CE modifier to deal one additional damage dice per cursed energy spent. Objects and structures within range take maximum damage. After using this, you fall under the effects of Technique Burnout until the end of your next turn.

Domain Expansion: Il Gran Dolce
Finally, at 18th level, you have honed your technique to the maximum, gaining your domain expansion. While inside it, at Initiative 20, you can choose up to three targets to suffer the full effects of Granite Blast.

While in Technique Burnout after your domain ends, you cannot use any Innate Technique features other than Granite Blast.

You can apply a circuit that allows for extremely efficient use of cursed energy.

Cursed Energy
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

Circuit
Starting at 1st level, as a bonus action for 2 Cursed Energy, you can apply a Circuit to yourself or an object you touch for 1 minute. You can also apply your Circuit to another willing creature you touch for 5 CE for half the time. Your cursed circuit gives the following:
Efficiency. The base cost of a feature that requires cursed energy other than Cursed Circuitry features decreases by 1 (min cost of 1). If a feature’s effects depend on how much cursed energy you spend, one cursed energy you spend gives the effects of two. (Eg. Spending 2 CE on Cursed Strike counts as 4 CE). This cannot cause the cursed energy to be higher than your output limit.
Output. When a feature allows you to spend additional cursed energy to strengthen the effects, you can spend additional cursed energy up to half to your proficiency bonus (rounded up).
Enhancement. If you apply your circuit onto an Object or Cursed Tool, it instead gains one of the following benefits of your choice:

  • The item deals an additional 2d4 necrotic damage on a hit.

  • The item grants a +2 bonus to AC

  • The cursed energy cost of the tool decreases by 1 (min of 1)

You can only have 1 circuit at a time. This becomes 2 circuits at 3rd level, 3 circuits at 6th, and 4 at 11th level.

Pure Energy Efficiency
At 3rd level, your technique has further increased in efficient functions. A creature under the effects of your Circuit, only lose 4 cursed energy for every 5 CE spent at once (Eg. target uses Hollow Purple for 10 CE, they cast it and only lose 8 CE).
High Performance Circuit
Starting at 6th level, you can now apply a high performing Circuit to yourself or an object you touch as a bonus action for 2 CE or a willing creature you touch for 5 CE. Your circuit now lasts for 1 hour or 10 minutes if applied to another creature.
Improved Efficiency. The base cost of a feature that requires cursed energy other than Cursed Circuitry features decreases by 3 (min cost of 1). If a feature’s effects depend on how much cursed energy you spend, 1 CE you spend counts as 3 CE (Eg. Spending 2 CE on Cursed Strike counts as 6 CE). This cannot cause the effective cursed energy to be higher than a feature’s output limit.
Increased Output. When a feature allows you to spend additional cursed energy to strengthen the effects, you can spend additional cursed energy up to your proficiency bonus.
Enhancement. If you apply your circuit onto an Object or Cursed Tool, it instead gains two of the following benefits of your choice:

  • The item deals an additional 2d6 necrotic damage on a hit, increasing to 2d10 at 11th level.

  • The item grants a +3 bonus to AC, increasing to +5 at 11th level.

  • The cursed energy cost of the tool decreases by 2 (min of 1). This instead decreases cost by 4 at 11th level.

Circuit Breaker
At 11th level, your Circuit now lasts for 8 hours or until you end it as a bonus action. Once per turn when one of your circuits ends, your next unarmed strike or attack with the item that held the circuit deals an additional 5d10 necrotic damage on a hit.

Domain Expansion: Deus ex Machina
At 18th level, you have mastered your technique allowing you to expand your domain. Within your domain, you are always under the effect of your Circuit. At initiative 20, creatures of your choice within your domain take necrotic damage equal to their current cursed energy as your domain saps their cursed energy into the circuit.

You create advanced cursed corpses that can function autonomously.

Cursed Energy
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

Cursed Corpse Creation
Starting at 1st level, your technique allows you to master the process of creating cursed corpses. A cursed corpse requires a cursed core to function, cursed energy for fuel, and a body. You start with either 2 completed tiny cursed corpses or 1 small cursed corpse.

Core. While you have enough money and access to materials, you can create up to a Small core as part of a long rest. At 3rd level, you can make a Medium Core, a Large at 6th level, Huge at 11th level, and Gargantuan at 18th level.

Cursed Core Size | Cost | Max Cursed Energy

Tiny Core | $5,000 | 10
Small Core | $30,000 | 25
Medium Core | $100,000 | 50
Large Core | $250,000 | 75
Huge Core | $500,000 | 100
Gargantuan Core | $1,000,000 | 150

Imbuement. While you have a core, you can imbue the core with cursed energy, allowing it to animate. You can imbue cursed energy into a core you touch as an action and grant it any amount of your cursed energy. However as shown in the table above it has a maximum amount it can handle. If the corpse uses cursed energy it comes from this pool and must be recharged by you. A tiny or small cursed corpse expends 1 CE for each day it is active. A medium or large consumes 5, huge consumes 10, and gargantuan consumes 20.
Body. The third thing you need is a body. The amount of materials and time needed for your cursed corpse is defined by its size. Your cursed corpse requires a core with a size matching the body. You can create up to a Small Cursed Corpse. At 3rd level, you can make a Medium Cursed Corpse, a Large at 6th level, Huge at 11th level, and Gargantuan at 18th level.

Cursed Corpse Size | Cost | Time

Tiny Cursed Corpse | $1,000 worth of materials | 30 min
Small Cursed Corpse | $10,000 worth of materials | 3 hours
Medium Cursed Corpse | $50,000 worth of materials | 24 hours
Large Cursed Corpse | $75,000 worth of materials | 72 hours
Huge Cursed Corpse | $100,000 worth of materials | 216 hours
Gargantuan Cursed Corpse | $150,000 worth of materials | 648 hours

Completed Cursed Corpse. After building your cursed corpse, it will use the following depending on what size it is. The cursed corpse inherits your proficiency bonus at the time of its creation. They regain their health normally on a short or long rest, and cannot be healed using Reversed Cursed Technique.
Cursed corpses are created for a niche and you allocate their stats during creation. Each score is a 6 before allocation and you have 27 points that you allocate between scores. Every increase costs 1 point, except for 14 and above, which cost 2 points each. The maximum score is as follows:

Ability | Tiny | Small | Medium | Large | Huge | Gargantuan |

Strength | 12 | 14 | 16 | 18 | 20 | 24 |
Dexterity | 18 | 16 | 14 | 12 | 10 | 8 |
