Charisma | 10 | 9 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 6 |

You can command a number of cursed corpses up to your proficiency bonus as a bonus action to act on your turn to have them act. Additionally, you can command the same number of cursed corpses as an action to give them a complex command that allows them to function for much longer as long as they are following that command. A Cursed Corpse with the Autonomy Mutation does not require commands to act, but can be commanded as a free action on your turn.

Corpse Tactics
At 3rd level, you have learned new ways to command your cursed corpses during combat. You can use one of these tactics as part of the bonus action you take to command your Cursed Corpses and lasts until the start of your next turn.

Cooperative Tactics. You give one of your Cursed Corpses advantage on an attack or saving throw on their turn.
Offensive Tactics. You cause one of your Cursed Corpses to deal an additional damage die on a hit.
Defensive Tactics. You let one of your Cursed Corpses take the Dodge action as a bonus action.
Guerilla Tactics. You let one of your cursed Corpses take the Disengage action as a bonus action.
Mobility Tactics. You let one of your Cursed Corpses take the Dash action as a bonus action.

Cursed Corpse Mutation
Starting at 6th level, your strong cursed energy has caused mutations to form. When you complete a cursed corpse, you roll a d20. On a roll of 20, your cursed corpse gains a random mutation.

D12 Roll | Mutation | Effect

1 | Quick Movement | Gains +20 ft bonus to walking speed.
2 | Adaptive Movement| Gains 30 ft climb or swim speed.
3 | Skills | Prof in 2 skills or 1 saving throw.
4 | Hardened Frame | Gains +3 bonus to AC.
5 | Weapon Usage | Can wield weapons proficiently.
6 | Toughness | Max HP increases by 2 x your level.
7 | Energy Capacity | One core can hold +30 additional CE.
8 | Energy Usage | Can use Basic CE Manipulation.
9 | Improved Ability | Gains +4 to an Ability and Max.
10 | Autonomy | Doesn’t require commands (sentient).
11 | Core Capacity | Can hold 1d4 additional cores.
12 | Self Generation | Regains 1 CE per hour.

Maximum: Prized Creation
At 11th level, you can put extra time and care into one of your favorite cursed corpses to make a masterpiece. You can choose one of your existing Cursed Corpses or when you make a new Cursed Corpse to be your Favorite. It gains the following:

  • It gains a +4 bonus to two of its Ability scores and their maximums for that score.

  • The damage die of all its attacks increases by one tier (D10<D12<2d8).

  • It gains 3 Mutations of your choice. You cannot select the same Mutation multiple times.

Perfect Creations
At 18th level, you can command all Cursed Corpses under your control as a bonus action on your turn regardless of numbers or distance. Additionally, your Cursed Corpses can continue functioning for a week after running out of cursed energy.

This power is called both a blessing and a curse, you can speak your will to reality.

Cursed Energy
At 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.
You regain all spent cursed energy on a long rest.

Power of Words
Starting at 1st level, you have been born with the Inumaki clan’s snake eyes and fangs seal on you, and can now curse other people just by merely speaking. However, this takes extreme strain on your vocal cords. Your vocal cords have a number of hit points equal to 1/3rd of your maximum hit points(rounded up). You are unable to speak unless in terms of whatever meaningless concept you choose such as sushi ingredients. For every Cursed Energy you spend in a cursed word, your vocal cords lose one hit point. Your vocal cords hit points all come back in a short or long rest. If your vocal chords reach 0 hit points, you won't be able to regain the hit points unless you receive hit points from Reverse Cursed Technique or take a long rest. If you have 0 hit points you cannot use your cursed words, and will always be under one level of exhaustion. Your vocal cords will regain 1 hit point at the beginning of your turns unless they are at 0 hit points. Any kind of hit point gain you receive affects your vocal cords' hit points. You can the Cursed Words below(X=Cursed Energy Mod):

  • Sleep: Replace one of your attacks for 1 Cursed Energy to cast Sleep at 1st level. You can add 3d8 per 1 extra Cursed Energy added at 3rd, 6th, 11th, and 18th levels.

  • Return: As an attack, for 1 Cursed Energy, you make a summoned creature within 60 ft make a Charisma save against your save DC or be unsummoned. At 3rd, 6th, 11th, and 18th levels you can choose to spend +1 Cursed Energy for +1 to DC.

  • Run Away: As an attack, for 2 Cursed Energy, you force one creature within 60 ft to run away from you, but not into harm. At 3rd, 6th, 11th, and 18th levels you can choose to spend +1 CE for +1 to DC or +1 target per Cursed Energy.

  • Blast Away: As an attack for 4 cursed energy, you force one target to make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, they are launched 60 ft back from the spot they were in, taking 1d8 force damage per 10ft traveled. At 3rd level, you can spend 1 additional Cursed Energy to add +10 to the distance the target is blasted away. You can spend another +1 at 6th, 11th, and 18th.

  • Plummet: As an action for 6 Cursed Energy, you force a target to make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, take Xd10 force damage and are knocked prone for 1 minute as a field of intensified gravity crushes them. They remove the prone condition if they succeed on a Strength saving throw on their turn. At 3rd level, you can spend +1 CE for additional Xd10 force damage. You can spend another +1 at 6th, 11th, and 18th. (X = CE modifier)

  • Get Twisted: As an action for 8 Cursed Energy, you force a target to make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure one of their legs or arms of your choice will be twisted, breaking the limb. In addition, the target will lose hit points equal to their Constitution score times half your proficiency bonus(rounded down). An arm twisted removes the ability to use that arm and reduces the creature’s Strength by 2, and twisting a leg halves movement and reduces Dexterity by 2. At 3rd level, you can spend 1 additional Cursed Energy to add a +1 to the DC. You can spend another +1 at 6th, 11th, and 18th levels.

  • Get Crushed: As an action for 10 Cursed Energy, you force a target to make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, they are imploded which makes them lose xd12 maximum hit points and become paralyzed. They will keep being imploded for 1 minute, this can be ended early if they succeed on a Strength saving throw, on a failure they will keep losing xd12 of their maximum hit points at the beginning of their turns. The hit points lost will be regained at the end of a long rest. At 3rd level, you can spend 1 additional Cursed Energy to add a d12 to the amount of hit points lost. You can spend another +1 at 6th, 11th, and 18th levels.

  • Don't Move: As an action for 12 Cursed Energy, you cast Power Word Stun at 8th level. You increase the HP limit by 25 HP per 1 point of Cursed Energy added at 3rd, 6th, 11th, and 18th levels.

  • Explode: As an action for 14 Cursed Energy, you force a target and every creature within 5ft. of it to make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, they will explode from the inside out making them receive 3d8 force damage + xd6 fire damage. At 3rd level, you can spend 1 additional Cursed Energy to add a d8 to the force damage. You can spend another +1 at 6th, 11th, and 18th levels.

  • Die: As an action for 16 Cursed Energy, you force a target with 30 times your Cursed Energy modifier hit points or less to make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, they die instantly. At 3rd level, you can spend 1 additional Cursed Energy to add a +1 to the DC and 10 hit points to the requirement. You can spend another +1 at 6th, 11th, and 18th levels.

Interjection
Beginning at 3rd, you have learned how to say one specific word quicker than the others. You can choose one of your cursed words to use as a Bonus Action or Reaction. You can change the chosen word at the end of a long rest.

Iron Chords
When you reach 6th level, due to the constant usage of your vocal cords, they have gotten stronger. Your vocal cords' hit points increase to half your maximum hit points(rounded up).

Resounding Voice
At 11th level, you can spend 3 extra Cursed Energy to change the effect range of your technique into a 35-foot cone.

Domain Expansion: Echo Chamber
If you reach 18th level, you have honed your technique to a fine edge, gaining your domain expansion. While inside it, at Initiative 20, you can make all creatures fall under the effect of a word of your choice for no cost.

You are blessed with an amazing technique to control Cursed Spirits.

Cursed Energy
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.
You regain all spent cursed energy on a long rest.

Cursed Spirit Absorption
Beginning at 1st level, you know the taste that no one will ever know, the taste of curses. As an action or reaction for 1 Cursed Energy, you exorcise a cursed spirit with 0 hit points, or a cursed spirit whose CR is less than your proficiency bonus within 120 ft that you can see and transform its soul into a small orb for you to eat. After that, you can summon it as an ally to fight for you. You can summon Cursed Spirits as an action by spending Cursed Energy equal to their CR. You can summon a number of cursed spirits as an action equal to your Cursed Energy modifier within 10 ft. They lose their free will and follow every command you give them. If reduced to 0 hit points they die and cannot be revived. They cannot use actions on their own. You must spend a bonus action to command each cursed spirit to attack, use cursed techniques, or do something more specific, such as 'protect that creature, grab that, kill that, etc. You can unsummon any number of curses as a bonus action, provided they are within line of sight.
You can only consume orbs without physical detriments if the curse has a CR lower or equal to your level. If you try to eat an orb out of a creature with a CR higher than your level, you must roll a DC 5 + the creature's CR Constitution Saving Throw. On a success, you absorb the curse and can use it after a short or long rest. On a fail, you gain 2 levels of exhaustion and receive Xd12 Necrotic Damage (X = curse CR) and cannot absorb it.
You're also able to absorb other sorcerer's cursed spirits as long as you kill the master first. You can have any number of cursed spirits, but for every 10 cursed spirits you consume, you must make a DC 10 Wisdom saving throw. On a success, you will gain no aftereffects. On a failure, you will gain a level of exhaustion or two exhaustion levels if you fail the save by 5 or more. This becomes three levels of exhaustion if you fail the save by 10 or more.

Curse Infused Spirits
Once you reach 3rd level, your Cursed Energy increases the power of your Cursed Spirits in the following ways:

  • Their Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution scores will gain a bonus equal to your Cursed Energy modifier.

  • They regain all HP at the end of a short rest.

  • They become immune to the frightened or charmed condition.

  • Regardless of distance, you'll know if your cursed spirits were exorcised.

  • In addition, as a reaction for x Cursed Energy you can sacrifice a cursed spirit in exchange for reducing incoming damage by xd20, with x being the CR of the creature sacrificed in the process.

Perfect Control
At 6th level, you have grown experienced with your cursed technique, giving you perfect control over your spirits and gain the following benefits:

  • The amount of cursed spirits it takes for you to make a Wisdom saving throw increases to 20.

  • Your cursed spirits cost is reduced by your Cursed Energy modifier (minimum cost of 1 CE).

  • Your DC for eating cursed spirits with a CR higher than your level is decreased by your Cursed Energy modifier

  • You can now summon cursed spirits as a bonus action.

Maximum: Uzumaki
When you reach 11th level, as an action you can put any number of your cursed spirits in a spiral-like pattern(minimum 2), making them into a dark spiral that you can use in an attack. Every creature in a 30-foot cone must make a Dexterity saving throw, on a success they take half damage, on a failure they take 2d12 Necrotic damage.
For every cursed spirit above 2, the area of effect will be increased by 5 feet, and the damage will increase by 1d12.
All of the cursed spirits that were used in the Uzumaki are killed. However, you can obtain the actions(including legendary actions)they have at a cost which must be paid when extracting them via Uzumaki. You can extract multiple actions from different curses as part of the process, but you must pay the cost for each action.
The cost for the actions is listed below and once extracted, the action can be used only once:

Action Type Cursed Energy Cost
Bonus Action 3
Action 4
Reactions 5
Legendary Actions 10

Domain Expansion: Womb Profusion
Finally at 18th level, you have learned how to expand your domain. A tree of souls surrounded by four seated Buddhas at the cardinal points emerges behind you, as your barrier starts opening. The area targeted by this feature counts as difficult terrain for all creatures. You can use any of your cursed spirits without any cost. Cursed spirits within your domain must make a Charisma saving throw at the beginning of their turns or be instantly absorbed by you.

You can change form, nature, and substance through your technique.

Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. Basic Transmutation
Starting at 1st level, you have learned to use your technique to alter the properties of items you touch. As an action you can spend an amount of cursed energy up to your Cursed Energy modifier to alter the shape or properties of a nonliving object you touch.
For each cursed energy point spent, you can affect up to a 5 ft cube of material per cursed energy spent (Metal costs an additional CE per cube). You can reshape the affected material in any way that fits within its original volume, allowing you to create cover, create difficult terrain, block passages, form platforms, or otherwise reposition the material to aid movement. At 6th level you can spend up to twice your Cursed Energy modifier, three times at 11th and four times at 18th.

A Transmuted Object has an AC of 10 and 5 hit points per 5 ft cube affected. The object’s durability increases if transmuting one of the following, as shown below:

  • Wood: +1 AC and +10 hit points per cube

  • Earth: +2 AC and +15 hit points per cube

  • Stone: +3 AC and +20 hit points per cube

  • Metal: +4 AC and +30 hit points per cube

Transmuted Objects automatically fail Strength and Dexterity saving throws and are immune to poison and psychic damage.

Chemical Formulae
At 3rd level, you have studied the structure of your technique and learned greater ways to utilize it:

Transmute Explosion. On a hit with a weapon attack, you can spend 2 cursed energy to transmute the attack and force the creature to make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 2d6 fire damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful save. This increases to 3d6 at 6th level, 4d6 at 11th level and 6d6 at 18th level.
Transmute Self. As a reaction, you can spend cursed energy to transmute yourself in one of the following ways (X = CE modifier):

  • Harden (2 CE) You harden your body and gain a +4 bonus to AC until the start of your turn.

  • Shell (X CE) You create a shell over your body and gain 5 temporary hit points per cursed energy spent.

  • Slick (2 CE) You cover parts of your body in a solution and gain a 20 ft bonus to walking speed and do not provoke opportunity attacks until the start of your turn.

Areal Transmute
At 6th level, you have learned to change the properties of larger areas. As an action for 6 cursed energy, you can transmute the ground beneath you in a radius of up to 30 ft in the following ways:
Slippery. You coat the area in a solution, forcing all creatures other than yourself to make a Dexterity saving throw or fall prone.
Explosive. You destabilize the ground by adding protons. As an action on your next turn, you release an explosion forcing all creatures in range (including you) to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, a creature takes 4d6 fire damage or half as much on a success. This increases to 6d6 at 11th level and 8d6 at 18th level.
Spikey. You form physical spikes in the area. A creature that walks 5 ft through this area takes 2d4 piercing damage.
Shifting. You form random foot falls and hazards in the area, causing it to become difficult terrain.

Maximum: Railgun
Starting at 11th level, you can compress matter and cursed energy into a hyper-accelerated projectile, launching it at a deafening velocity.
As an action, you spend 8 cursed energy and transmute a small piece of nonliving material you can touch or that is on your person into a railgun slug. Choose a point or creature you can see within 120 feet to be the target and make a ranged cursed energy attack against them

On a hit, the target takes 8d12 piercing damage or half as much damage if the attack misses and must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your Cursed Energy save DC or be pushed up to 30 feet directly away from you and knocked prone. If the target impacts another object or structure it takes 2d12 bludgeoning damage. Objects and structures in the projectile’s path automatically take twice as much damage and are destroyed if reduced to 0 hit points. A creature in the projectile’s path must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 4d12 thunder damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

Domain Expansion: Mandala of Dependant Origination
At 18th level you have mastered your technique allowing you to expand your domain. At initiative 20, your entire domain is affected by an Areal Transmute of your choice and takes effect immediately. Additionally, you can use Transmute Self on willing creatures within your domain.

The technique you have is made for one purpose, justice.

Cursed Energy
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

Judge’s Gavel
At 1st level, once per long rest, you can summon a magical gavel for free once per long rest. Otherwise, you can spend 1 Cursed Energy to resummon it to your hand. This weapon has 3 forms: a base form a light hammer, maul, and pole hammer (Reach, d10).

Domain Expansion: Deadly Sentencing
Beginning at 3rd level, your will lets you expand your domain for free once per long rest. Within the domain, no offensive action can be taken by either party. The target must make a contested Persuasion check against you to prove their innocence. You gain a piece of Evidence determined by a d20 roll. If you succeed, they suffer the punishment based on your Evidence for 1 minute and the domain ends.

Roll Evidence
1 Innocent: The person is innocent but accused of a heinous crime which is easily excusable. You fail unless the defendant admits to it for some reason, if so a dependent punishment can apply.
2-9 Guilty: The person is guilty of a small crime with minimum evidence, your roll is normal. Confiscation
10-15 Very Guilty: The person is guilty of a crime, and you have good evidence, your roll is at advantage. Confiscation
15-19 Severely Guilty: The person is guilty of a severe crime, and you have decent evidence. Death Penalty
20 Unforgivably Guilty: The person is guilty beyond a doubt of an unforgivable sin, you instantly succeed. Death Penalty, Confiscation

Confiscation: The target loses either their innate technique or any magic items(items first). A creature without loses their CE.
Death Penalty: Your Judge’s Gavel is replaced by the Executioner’s Sword which instantly kills the accused on a hit.
Your DM may impose bonuses or penalties to Evidence rolls if fitting.
Your domain is Non-Lethal and instead of a guaranteed hit, gains the benefits of Peace Treaty as listed in Non-Lethal Domains. If you manage to convict a target with Confiscation or Death Penalty, you are not affected by Technique Burnout when your domain ends.

Gavel Improvements
Starting at 6th level, your mastery over Judge’s Gavel has improved. You can now re-summon your gavel as a free action. You can also spend 2 CE to increase the size of the gavel for 1 minute. The damage dice increase by one tier (d8<d10<d12<2d8). As an action, you can swing the enlarged gavel down on a 10 feet diameter square within 5 feet of you, forcing creatures within range to make a Dexterity saving throw or take twice your gavel’s damage.

Better Evidence
At 11th level, when rolling for evidence you can roll two dice and pick the one you find more beneficial. This becomes 3 at 18th level.

Unstopping Justice
Finally, at 18th level, you have reached the peak of your technique, showing off to others that only with skill you can truly win. You can now use Deadly Sentencing a number of times equal to your CE modifier without spending Cursed Energy each long rest.

World Anchor

Domain Expansion: Trichiliocosm
At 18th level you have learned to expand your domain. At initiative 20, all creatures of your choice within your domain take 6d12 bludgeoning damage and are restrained by shifting stone until the start of their next turn.
You can spend an action to change the environment of your domain.

  • You can create a large 20 ft radius, 1d10 x 10 feet deep chasm causing creatures to fall and take falling damage.

  • You can create a 100 ft tall tower of stone (as if casting Galdur’s Tower with 10 stories).

One of your ancestors devoured Yamata no Orochi, the Eight Headed Serpent, creating a hereditary technique with its power.

The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

Eight Lives
Starting at 1st level, you have the ability to come back to life after you die, up to 8 times. When you are reduced to 0 hit points or die outright, you can spend 1 CE to come back to life at half your hitpoint maximum and harmful conditions other than exhaustion are removed. You have 8 lives and can use a life this way three times per long rest. This increases to four at 3rd level and eight at 6th level. You regain one expended life after eight days.

Collective Will
At 3rd level, when you make an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma ability check or saving throw, you can spend 1 cursed energy to reroll and must use the new roll. You can use this feature up to 8 times per long rest.
Fangs of Orochi
At 6th level, as an action you can spend up to 8 cursed energy to summon an equal number of fangs from the jaws of Yamata no Orochi as shikigami. They appear in unoccupied spaces of your choice within 10 ft. You can have up to 8 summoned at a time.

Maximum: Sacrifice

A barrier forms, connecting the Fangs like a cylinder resembling a trigram and trapping any within.

The barrier has a height of 20 ft and can have a maximum diameter of 15 ft. It has 20 AC and hit points equal to the hit points of the Fangs of Orochi used to create it. A trapped creature makes a cursed energy save at the start of their turns, taking 10d4 necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful save.

If this damage reduces a humanoid to 0 hit points, the creature dies and you regain one life. Once you regain a life in this way, you cannot for 1 week.
Domain Expansion: Ama ga Fuchi
Finally at 18th level, you have constructed a domain filled with your technique. The domain takes the form of grassy wetlands. At initiative 20, Yamata no Orochi forms from the earth. The shikigami does not take actions and does not have a turn in initiative. This is a false incarnation that only exists within your domain, containing the shackled mind of the original Yamata no Orochi.
On initiative 20 after Yamata no Orochi has formed, roll a 1d8. That number of creatures of your choice within the domain each suffer its bite. The shikigami disappears when your domain ends.

You were born with the ability to create cursed paintings leading to unique subspaces.

Cursed Energy
Beginning at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. Cursed Painting
Starting at 1st level, you can spend 1 cursed energy to create a painting of cursed ink under a Medium or smaller creature within 30 ft, forcing them to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they are sucked into the painting. The painting takes the form of an empty 30 ft radius cube subspace of greyscale. You can change the color or create simple illustrations within the subspace as an action. You can enter, exit, place, or remove an item from the subspace of your paintings as a free action once per turn without spending cursed energy. Your subspace becomes 120 ft at 3rd level, 600 ft at 6th, and 1200 ft at 11th level.

At the beginning of your turn, you must spend 1 CE to keep any creatures (including yourself) within a painting. Otherwise, they reappear at the point they disappeared.

You can use a binding vow to remove the cost at the beginning of your turn by placing a method of escape. This creates an Exit Painting in a random, but accessible area within the subspace that allows a creature to exit the painting, reappearing in the space they disappeared.

You can have a number of subspaces equal to your CE modifier, but if you have creatures in different paintings, you must spend 1 cursed energy for each subspace at the start of your turn. This increases to twice your CE modifier of paintings at 11th level.

Alternatively, you can paint a physical painting and imbue it with up to 3 cursed energy during its creation, spending 1 hour painting per cursed energy. A creature that gets within 5 ft and can see the painting must make a Dexterity saving throw, getting sucked into the painting on a failed save. A painting imbued this way keeps a creature trapped for 3 rounds. The painting’s subspace can only be accessed through the physical painting.

At 3rd level, you can spend additional cursed energy up to your Cursed Energy modifier to imbue the painting with more power and increase the painting time. This increases to twice your CE modifier at 11th level. This allows the painting to keep an unwilling creature trapped for an additional round for every cursed energy spent. You can also use this painting to store items, but it also counts against the number of paintings you can have at once.

At 6th level, you can instead cause the painting to spend the imbued cursed energy to use Ink Wave against a creature that moves within 5 ft of it.

Impasto Canvas
At 3rd level, you gain the ability to change the content of one of your paintings in one the following ways while within your painting:
Ink Shikigami. As an action, you can spend up to your Cursed Energy modifier to create one Ink Wolf for each cursed energy spent. Each wolf appears in an unoccupied space you can see anywhere within your painting and acts on your initiative. The wolves obey your verbal commands (no action required).
Exit Shift. You move the Exit Painting up to 80 ft as an action.
Difficult Terrain. As an action, you create a 15 ft radius area of difficult terrain anywhere within your painting. The terrain lasts until the painting ends or until you use this feature again.
Structure Generation. As an action, you create one structure from cursed ink anywhere within your painting. The structure must fit entirely within a 30 ft cube and can be any ordinary structure you choose, such as walls, platforms, towers, bridges, or buildings.
The structure’s AC equals your CE save DC and each 5 ft by 5 ft section has hit points equal to 5 x your proficiency bonus.
If reduced to 0 hit points, it dissolves into ink and disappears. Any creatures standing on the structure when it is destroyed fall or are affected at the DM’s discretion. You can create, destroy, or replace a structure while within the painting.
Trap Creation. As an action, you create one trap of your choice in an unoccupied 5 ft square anywhere within your painting. The trap lasts until triggered or until the painting ends. A creature can detect a trap with an Intelligence (Investigation) or Wisdom (Perception) check against your Cursed Energy save DC. All traps use your CE save DC.:

  • Pit Trap. When a creature enters the trapped space, it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or fall 20 feet into the pit, taking 2d6 bludgeoning damage and falling prone.

  • Spike Trap. When a creature enters the trapped space, it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or fall 10 feet into the pit, taking 2d10 piercing damage and falling prone.

  • Snare Trap. When a creature enters the trapped space, it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or become restrained. A creature can use its action to make a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check, freeing the target on a success.

  • Rolling Stone Trap. When triggered, an ink-formed boulder rolls in a 5 ft wide 30 ft line from the trap’s space in a direction you choose. Each creature in the line must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 4d10 bludgeoning damage and knocked prone on a fail, or half as much damage and not prone on a success.

Sgraffito
At 6th level, you have improved your technique. You can now manipulate your painting as a bonus action and gain the following improvements and options:
Ink Shikigami. You can summon new types of shikigami:
Greater Ink Wolf (2 CE)
Ink Crow (3 CE)
Exit Shift. You cause the location of the Exit Painting to a new random accessible location in the subspace.
Difficult Terrain. You can now create a 30 ft radius area of difficult terrain anywhere within your painting.
Structure Generation. Each 5 ft by 5 ft section of a structure you create now has hit points equal to 10 x your proficiency bonus.
Trap Creation. Your traps now deal an additional 2 damage dice. This increases to an additional 4 damage dice at 11th level.
Ink Wave. As an action for 2 cursed energy, you create a 30 ft cone originating from you or an Ink Shikigami. A creature within the cone must make a Constitution saving throw, taking your proficiency bonus in d6s of necrotic damage and be blinded until the end of their next turn on a failed save. (This can also be used outside your subspace)
Larger Frames. You can now use Cursed Painting on Large or smaller creatures. This increases to Huge at 11th level.

Panoramic Composition
At 11th level, as an action, you can spend cursed energy up to twice your CE modifier, forcing that number of creatures within 60 ft to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they are sucked into your cursed paintings.

Domain Expansion: Magnum Opus
At 18th level you have learned to expand your domain. The inside of your domain counts as your painting’s subspace, expanding to the same size as your subspace and following the same rules, except your Ink Shikigami and Traps are imbued with your guaranteed hit. At initiative 20, two different Impasto Canvas effects of your choice happen (if you choose Ink Shikigami, they still cost Cursed Energy).

Self-Destruction
Starting at 1st level, you can make any part of you a deadly bomb. You spend cursed energy to remove and throw your body parts. You remove the part as described below. Throwing takes an action:

Attack Cost Action Effect
Tiny(Tooth, Finger, Hair) 1 CE + Con mod HP Free action You throw the body part at a point within 120ft. Creatures within 5 ft make a Dex save. On a failure, they take Xd6 force damage. On a success, they take half.
Small(Ears, Nose) 2 CE + Con mod×half your level HP Bonus action You throw the body part at a point within 100ft. Creatures within 10 ft make a Dex save. On a failure, they take Xd8 force damage and are knocked prone. On a success they take half.
Medium(Hands, Feet) 4 CE + Con mod×level HP Action You throw the body part at a point within 80ft. Creatures within 15 ft make a Dex save. On a failure, they take Xd10 force damage and are knocked prone. On a success, they take half.

Faster Throws
At 3rd level, you have gained more expertise over your technique, and can now throw your bombs faster. You can now throw a body part as an action or bonus action.

Guerilla Tactics
At 6th level, your practice with your explosions allowed you to make them in an instant. You can now instantly explode one of your body parts for the normal cost, as a reaction to receiving or hitting a melee attack roll as the body part explodes on your body. All creatures make the Dexterity saving throw with disadvantage unless their passive perception is higher than your cursed energy DC.

Stronger Explosions
At 11th level, with the extensive use of your technique, your explosions became deadlier. When a creature fails the saving throw of your explosions, they gain the deafened condition for 1 minute. They can make a Constitution saving throw at the beginning of their turns, ending the condition early on a success. Also, your explosions deal three times as much damage to objects and structures and their explosion range is increased by 5ft.
At 18th level, the creature also gains the blinded condition.

Domain Expansion: True Art
At 18th level, you have mastered your technique, allowing you to expand your domain. You can detonate any of your body parts for no CE cost. At initiative 20, you can choose a limb (arm or leg) from a creature inside your domain and detonate it.

You can store and release kinetic energy using your cursed technique.

Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. Starting at 1st level, you can store and release energy. When you miss with a melee attack, you gain a Jin charge. You can have a number of Jin charges equal to your proficiency bonus + your level.
You can spend a Jin charge or 1 Cursed Energy to either gain a +2 to a melee or cursed energy attack roll or deal an additional damage die for each charge spent.
You must declare how many Jin charges you are using before making an attack or using a technique and can use a number of Jin charges equal to your proficiency bonus at once. On a miss, you waste the Jin charges. You lose all unused Jin charges on a long rest.

Instantaneous Movement

Fist of Explosive Power

Attack Effect
Unarmed or Bludgeoning 15 feet cone, Con save, 2D6 bludgeoning damage per Jin charge, knocked prone on a failed save
Slashing or Piercing 30 feet line, Dex save, 2D10 slashing damage per Jin charge

Maximize Potential Energy
At 11th level, you have learned not only how to avoid wasting your stored energy, but how to use it more effectively, granting you the following benefits:

  • When you spend Jin charges to enhance an attack and miss, you can keep a number of Jin charges up to your Cursed Energy modifier instead of losing the charges.

  • When you spend at least 3 Jin charges for Explosive Power, you can increase the range of your compressed air blast by 30 feet, which now deals thunder damage.

  • When you spend ce to gain a Jin charge, you now gain 2 Jin charges for every ce spent.

  • As an action while touching a creature, you can give them a number of your Jin charges up to your CE modifier.

Domain Expansion: Hall of Divine Bagua
At 18th level, you have learned your domain. Within your domain, you have unlimited Jin charges and at initiative 20, all creatures within your domain gain a permanent negative Jin charge, causing them to deal 1d6 less damage on their next attack or technique for each charge. These charges disappear when your domain ends.

Madness Inducement
Starting at 1st level, just looking at you slowly leads to mental corruption. As an action for 3 cursed energy, you can activate your technique for 1 minute causing madness to spread to everyone around you. If a creature ends their turn within 60 ft of you and can see you, it gains a 5% increase to Mental Corruption. You can choose a number of creatures to be immune to this effect when you activate the technique.

Corruption Rate Effect
10% -1 to AC

Paranoia and Madness. When a creature reaches 25% Mental Corruption, they begin seeing all creatures as faceless monsters and must roll a d10 at the start of their turn. On a roll of 1-2, the target spends their action attacking the closest creature. A creature can only have up to 25% Mental Corruption at a time.

Madness Removal. Mental Corruption persists even after your technique has been deactivated. A creature without line of sight to you can make a Wisdom saving throw to reduce Mental Corruption by 5% and repeat the save at the beginning of their turn. As part of a long rest, they can attempt to make a Wisdom saving throw to cleanse their mind. On a success, they can begin making saves to reduce madness as normal, down to the next 25% segment before they must complete another long rest to repeat the save and continue to process.

Madness Enhancement
At 3rd level, you learn to directly inject madness into a creature. Once per turn, when you hit a creature with a melee attack while your technique is active, they gain a 5% increase to Mental Corruption. You can spend additional cursed energy up to your proficiency bonus on a hit to increase Mental Corruption by 5% per cursed energy spent.

Obsession and Insanity
At 6th level, the percent of Mental Corruption you can force on a creature increases to 50% and increases by 25% again at 11th level and 18th level. The die size for Paranoia and Madness decreases with every 25% increase and at 100% it happens automatically. At 90% you fall further into madness and must make a Wisdom saving throw at the beginning of your turn, moving in a random direction on a failed save.

Maximum: Rumination
At 11th level, you can spend 6 cursed energy as an action to target a creature within 30 feet that you can see and is currently afflicted by your madness. The target must make an Intelligence saving throw or take 1d10 psychic damage per 10% Mental Corruption they currently have.
A creature with more than 50% Mental Corruption makes this save with disadvantage.
Domain Expansion: Theia Mania
Finally at 18th level, you have learned to expand your domain. At initiative 20, all creatures of your choice within your domain gains 5% Mental Corruption. Creatures gain a -1 penalty to all rolls for every 10% Mental Corruption they have while within your domain.

The wheel of fate is yours to steer and yours alone.

Cursed Energy
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

Fate Manipulation
Beginning at 1st level, you can weave together threads of fate. As an action for 2 cursed energy, you bind two creatures within 30 ft of you with an invisible red thread for 1 minute. If a Fate requires Touch, you must touch both targets, but not necessarily at the same time. You choose a Fate, +1 Fate per 2 additional CE, up to your proficiency bonus that affects both while within 30 ft of each other:

Fate Effect Requirement
Bonds The targets gain a +2 bonus to AC. N/A
Promised Time? The creatures both have either advantage or disadvantage on attacks against each other. N/A
Mirrored If one target rolls a 20 or 1 on their turn, the other’s next roll will be the opposite. N/A
Magnetic If targets start their turn within 30 ft of each other, they are pulled 10 ft closer. If this brings them within 5 ft, they become tangled and prone (Str save to pull away). Touch
Shared Strengths Choose a damage resistance, immunity, vulnerability or condition immunity of a target. Both targets share that strength/weakness. 6th level
Linked Suffering When one of the linked targets takes damage, they take half as much damage and the linked creature takes the other half. 6th level, Touch
Destined Death The targets both have either advantage or disadvantage on saves against each other. 11th level, Touch

An effect that would damage the soul is capable of cutting your thread and removing your technique’s effects. Additionally, you cannot manipulate the fate of a creature that is completely lacking cursed energy (such as via Heavenly Restriction).

Cursed Eyes of Fate
At 3rd level, you learn that fate is not simple. It is what makes up all connections between people and everything else. As a bonus action for 1 CE, when you look at a creature you can focus until you see the red threads of fate that connect the souls of all living creatures. As part of this bonus action, you can tell who the threads connect to if they are within sight, as well as the type of connection. This can range from familial connections, admiration, or feelings of love.
Alternatively, you can instead read the target’s personal thread of fate to learn one of the following:

  • The target’s damage resistances, immunities, or vulnerabilities.

  • The target’s CR or Level.

  • The target’s remaining hit points.

  • The target’s AC or an Ability modifier.

  • The target’s current emotions.

Strong Destiny
At 6th level, you have learned to strengthen your threads of fate with cursed energy. When you apply a fate to creatures, you can increase the duration by 1 minute per additional cursed energy spent. As a reaction to the target’s turn starting for 2 CE, you can cause a creature under one of your Fates to take Xd8 bludgeoning, slashing, or piercing damage (your choice) equaling your proficiency bonus as random unlucky phenomena assaults them. Additionally, the target must make a Dexterity saving throw or fall prone.
At 11th level, your Fate Manipulation now lasts for 1 hour and you can increase the duration by 1 hour per additional cursed energy spent.

Karmic Entanglement
At 11th level, you have learned to permanently entangle souls in the web of fate. Over an uninterrupted period of 1 week, you permanently intertwine the fates of two or more creatures together. The creatures become destined to meet by fate. You can attach this to an incredibly unique part of one of the creatures, such as Inherited Technique, Special Trait, or unique Constitution (Star Plasma Vessel) to cause it to be passed down even after the targets’ deaths. You can have a number of creatures with permanently intertwined fate equal to your proficiency bonus at once (including yourself).
Immortality. As a side effect of your technique, your fate has become set. You cannot die of old age, but still grow older. Every 500 years you must assimilate with a genetically similar human to reset your body and appearance. Failure to meet this causes you to begin to evolve beyond humanity, changing your race to Cursed Spirit.
Fate Control. As an action for 8 CE, you manifest fate for 1 minute. While active, you gain 3 fate points at the beginning of your turns. You can spend one fate point to add a -5 penalty to an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw made by a creature you can see within 30 ft (cannot stack). Unused fate points disappear at the start of your turn. While active, damage dice of Strong Destiny is doubled.

Domain Expansion: Road of Karma
Finally at 18th level, you have learned to expand your domain. At initiative 20, you select a creature within your domain as your Destined Foe. While your Destined Foe is within your domain, all your attacks against them are imbued with your guaranteed hit. You can switch your Destined Foe to another creature at initiative 20.

Your innate technique features count your domain as being within range and you can ignore the Touch Requirement of Fates.

You can conjure a pen-like cursed tool that lets you see the future.

Warstaff
Starting at 1st level, you can summon a pen-like cursed tool that allows you to see into the future of your opponents. As a bonus action for 2 cursed energy, you create an oversized pen-like cursed tool. This cursed tool has the reach and two-handed properties and you can use your CE modifier for its attack and damage rolls. On a hit it deals 1d4 + your CE modifier piercing damage and counts as a grade 4 cursed tool and can be used with martial arts die. You can dismiss the Warstaff at will and can only have one created at a time.

When you hit a creature with G Warstaff, you fulfill the condition for ink and attach a manga panel to the target, being able to view 1 second into the target's future. Hitting a target more than once adds another 1 second to the total, making you gain the benefits of the earlier seconds and the current. As a reaction or bonus action for 1 cursed energy, you can view that creature's future again and gain the following foresights until the beginning of your next turn depending on the creature’s marks. You cannot use this while blinded.

Seconds Foresight
1 Second The creature's attack rolls against you are made at disadvantage
2 Seconds You have advantage on saving throws from that creature
3 Seconds You have advantage on attack rolls against that creature
4 Seconds You know the next actions of the creature (The DM tells you at the start of their turn)
5 Seconds You know the next actions of the creature (The DM tells you at the end of your turn)
6 Seconds You know the next actions of the creature (The DM tells you at the beginning of your turn)

You can only see into a number of seconds into a creature's future equal to your proficiency bonus. The number of creatures that can be affected by this technique is equal to your CE modifier, and you can end the technique at will or it ends when the combat ends.
Highlighted Panels
At 3rd level, with the power of reading into the future, no one surprises you anymore. As long as you can see 2 seconds into a creature's future, you take half damage on a failure, and no damage on a success against saving throws caused by that creature.

Predictable Strikes
At 6th level, your opponents become extremely easy to read after being affected by your technique, and you learned how to exploit that. Once per turn when you hit an attack using G Warstaff against a creature that you can see 3 seconds into the future, you can turn that attack into a critical. You cannot roll for a black flash using this feature.

Precognition
At 11th level, you can glimpse your own future, knowing exactly what to do and when. When you roll with advantage against a creature because of your technique, your critical range is increased by half your CE modifier(rounded down).
Whenever a creature rolls with disadvantage against you because of your technique, the roll’s critical fail range is increased by half of your CE modifier(rounded down). For example, if you have a +4 CE modifier and they roll a natural 3 on their roll, it counts as a critical failure.

Domain Expansion: Storyboard Dominion
At 18th level, you have mastered your technique allowing you to expand your domain. All creatures in your domain count as having 6 seconds marked and at initiative 20, you can see 6 seconds into the future of all creatures.

Once per turn you can spend 2 additional CE to activate one of your technique features requiring an attack roll as a bonus action. Transfigured Creatures. You can have a number of transfigured creatures equal to your level x your Cursed Energy modifier. Alteration

Alteration CE Cost Description Restrictions

Body Clone

Your technique lets you curse people and make them see illusions.

Cursed Illusion
At 1st level, your technique allows you to curse creatures and make them see other people's faces in a distorted way. You are also able to track those you have cursed. As an action for 2 cursed energy, you can curse a creature within 60 feet. The target must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, the next person they see has a distorted face. Upon seeing this distortion for the first time, the creature must make an Intelligence saving throw. On a failure, the creature is confused and has disadvantage on attack rolls and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma checks until the end of their next turn. A sorcerer can repeat the Charisma save at the end of their turns to end the curse.
When a creature fails their Charisma saving throw, you gain the ability to track them up to 400 feet away. While a creature is cursed, you know its general location. The cursed creature keeps seeing the distorted face until they succeed the save or leave your tracking range.

Additionally, a creature that fails its save also has disadvantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saves and loses concentration on any technique or feature it was concentrating on.

Self Distortion
At 3rd level, you’ve learned how to distort your own body to confuse your opponents. You learn the 3 following distortion techniques:
Phase Fist. As part of making a melee attack, you can spend 3 cursed energy to create a duplicate of your weapon. Make a melee cursed attack roll at disadvantage, afterwards you make your normal attack against the same target. If the phase attack misses the actual attack will deal double the damage dice on a hit and if the phase attack hits the main attack will instead be made at advantage.
Blurring. As an action for 3 cursed energy, your body becomes blurred, shifting and wavering to all who can see you. An attacker is immune to this effect if it doesn't rely on sight like blindsight or can see through illusions like with true sight.

For example, if you use this technique to add a hat to your outfit, objects pass through the hat, and anyone who touches it would feel nothing or would feel your head and hair. To discern that you are disguised, a creature can use its action to inspect your appearance and must succeed on an Intelligence (Investigation) check against your cursed energy save DC.
Object Distortion
At 6th level, you have now learned a new way to distort the surroundings of those you have cursed. As an action, you may choose an object within the range of your cursed illusion that you can see to distort its appearance, this can include changing its opacity, luster, visible texture, or its seen value. A creature can attempt to discern the illusion by rolling an investigation check against your cursed energy save DC. You can spend an additional 3 CE to make the object invisible. If a creature runs into a medium or larger invisible object, they take 1d6 bludgeoning and lose their reaction.

Size CE Cost

  • Rough Ground. You make the terrain appear difficult to traverse, when a creature attempts to walk in this area they must spend twice as much movement per 5 ft of travel.

At 18th level, you have mastered your technique allowing you to open your domain. At initiative 20, you can force all creatures to fall under an illusion of your choice. Additionally, you can use your reaction to trick a creature that attacks you to target a random creature within range. You invert damage taken based on a specific threshold.

Cursed Energy
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

Inversion
Starting at 1st level, you gain the ability to invert the damage you take. As a bonus action, you can spend 2 cursed energy to activate Inverse for 1 minute. While Inverse is active, when you take damage, it is modified based on a damage limit and threshold. The damage limit equals your proficiency bonus times your Cursed Energy score, and the threshold is equal to your proficiency bonus times your Cursed Energy modifier.
When you take damage that exceeds your threshold, you subtract the threshold from the damage and take the remaining difference as damage. However, when the damage is below your threshold, you subtract the threshold from the damage and take the resulting number as damage instead. For example, if your set limit is 100 and you take 90 damage, you would subtract the damage from your limit if it exceeds the threshold (e.g., 90 - 20 = 70), and take the remaining 70 damage. Conversely, if the damage is below the threshold (e.g., 10 damage), you subtract that amount from your set limit (100 - 10 = 90), and take 90 damage instead. If the calculation results in a negative number, the damage remains unchanged.
You can extend the duration of Inverse by spending 1 cursed energy to maintain the effect for an additional minute.

Extreme Opposites
At 3rd level, you’ve learned to further manipulate the damage you take based on its intensity. If you take damage that is below your threshold, you are considered vulnerable to the damage dealt. However, if the damage exceeds your threshold, you gain resistance to the damage, even if it would normally bypass resistances or immunities.
For example, if your threshold is 15 and you take 10 damage, you treat that as vulnerability. But if you take 18 damage, you instead halve it due to your resistance, even if that type of damage would normally ignore resistances.

Break the Strong
At 6th level, you’ve become adept at manipulating damage based on its intensity, even when making saving throws. When you are forced to make a saving throw against an effect that deals damage, the difficulty of the save depends on whether the damage is above or below your threshold.
If the damage is above your threshold, you have advantage on the saving throw, regardless of the damage type. If the damage is below your threshold, you have disadvantage on the saving throw, as weaker attacks become more dangerous to you.
For example, if your threshold is 15 and you would take 18 damage from a fireball, you gain advantage on the saving throw. However, if you take 10 damage from the same attack, you would roll with disadvantage instead.

Quick Inversion
At 11th level, staying with your technique active for long periods of time can become a disadvantage at times, so you have trained to have easier access to your technique. You can now use your technique as a reaction to damage and can deactivate your technique as a reaction.
In addition, you now have additional reactions equal to half of your proficiency bonus(rounded up) that can be used only for the inverse technique. At 18th level, this becomes a number of reactions equal to your proficiency bonus.

Domain Expansion: Synesthesia
At 18th level, you have mastered your technique allowing you to open your domain. Within your domain, you can activate Inverse as a free action an infinite number of times for no cost. At initiative 20, creatures of your choice have their senses inverted. Each creature rolls a d4 (1: taste, 2: smell, 3: touch, 4: sight) having a sense inverted and unable to be used. A creature can make a Cursed Energy check at the end of their turn to regain their lost sense.

Domain Expansion: Laplace Threshold
